subject: SLA coverage review and remedy buckets — BlueCrest
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@bluecrest.io>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA review: uptime commitments and maintenance carveouts

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending the SLA template. We reviewed Redwood_SLA_Template_v3.pdf (attached) with our procurement and legal teams. A few points are blockers for BlueCrest to progress to signature: 

- Uptime: the template lists 99.9% as the standard uptime floor. For our customer-facing product we need 99.95% baseline (we examine >99.95% historically).
- Maintenance carveouts: the current carveout language allows scheduled maintenance without limits. We need either (a) a defined monthly limit on scheduled maintenance (no more than 6 hours/month for scheduled work) or (b) removal of broad scheduled carveouts for our production workloads.
- Latency SLOs: we need a P95 interactive latency guarantee of 150ms for the hosted inference endpoints used by our front-end (this is called out in our SOC-contracted operations).
- Credits: the credit matrix in your template calculates credits as a % of monthly fees but does not align with our procurement model. We require a predictable sliding scale: 10% credit for <99.95, 25% for <99.9, 50% for <99.5, with a cap at 40% per monthly invoice.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these points or propose a compromise. If helpful, I can loop in our legal counsel (cc: BlueCrest Legal) and procurement lead to accelerate redlines.

Attachments: BlueCrest_SLA_Redlines.docx (their annotated redlines)

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Procurement
BlueCrest Analytics

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@bluecrest.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA review: uptime commitments and maintenance carveouts

Hi Samira — thanks for the quick read and the attached redlines. Appreciate the clarity. 

High-level response and a proposed middle-ground so we can move toward contract execution: 

- Uptime: Redwood standard public-hosted API SLA is 99.9% for hosted tiers. For enterprise commitments we can make a targeted uplift: we can offer a 99.92% uptime floor for BlueCrest on a Dedicated plan (reserved capacity) with a 3-month performance review.

- Maintenance carveouts: rather than removing scheduled maintenance carveouts entirely, we can add a hard limit: scheduled maintenance impacting production endpoints will be capped at 6 hours per calendar month for BlueCrest (we will provide 48-hour advance notice for scheduled work). Emergency maintenance (unplanned mitigations) will be communicated and will not exceed 24 hours cumulative per month except in rare catastrophic events; we will provide root-cause analysis for anything longer.

- Latency: we can commit to P95 <= 200ms for interactive endpoints on the Dedicated capacity we propose. Reducing to 150ms is aggressive for the model sizes you indicated; we can include a performance SLT (service level target) at 150ms during a pilot if you commit to a specific model family and traffic profile so we can tune kernels and batching.

- Credits: propose a compromise on remedial credits: <99.92% = 10% monthly credit; <99.85% = 25% monthly credit; <99.5% = 50% monthly credit, with a monthly cap of 30% of the invoice. We will include an onboarding credit of $15,000 to offset initial ramp risk.

I've attached Redwood_SLA_Response_v1.pdf which highlights these points and the exact contract language we propose to add. If that looks reasonable, we can exchange redlines and route to legal for a quick DocuSign.

Cc'ing Ben and Marissa to help with credit impact and the dedicated capacity scoping. Happy to jump on a call this week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@bluecrest.io>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: BlueCrest Legal <legal@bluecrest.io>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA review: uptime commitments and maintenance carveouts

Laura — thanks for the fast reply and the clear counterproposal. A few clarifications / pushbacks from legal and procurement after reviewing Redwood_SLA_Response_v1.pdf: 

- 99.92% we can consider, but only if the scheduled maintenance cap is firm and measurable. Your 48-hour notice is reasonable; procurement insists on an SLA metric for scheduled maintenance hours (we want visibility via monthly report).
- Monthly cap of 30% is lower than our procurement model; we typically allow up to 40% for platform providers at this tier. We need Redwood to either move to 40% cap OR provide a better commercial concession in exchange (longer term commit, lower per-token fees, or a service credit escrow).
- Latency: BlueCrest can accept P95 <= 200ms as a baseline conditional on a 3-month pilot where we measure p95 at production volumes. If you want to claim a P95 150ms guarantee later, we need a performance certification milestone documented.

Attached are our annotated redlines (BlueCrest_SLA_Redlines.docx) with inline comments. Legal will not accept language that allows undefined 'emergency maintenance' to be used to avoid crediting — please add a definition and an approval gate (post-incident review with logs).

If you can confirm (a) a measurable scheduled maintenance cap with monthly reporting, and (b) a higher monthly credit cap to 40% or an offsetting commercial concession, we can move forward quickly.

Regards,
Samira

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Folks — forwarding Samira's note (below) and their redlines. Quick asks: 

1) Ben — can you model the financial exposure if we move the monthly credit cap from 30% to 40% for their projected ARR? Also show cost to us if we add a 6-hour scheduled maintenance hard cap and provide a monthly maintenance-hours report (operational cost and tooling).
2) Marissa — legal asks for a tight definition of "Emergency Maintenance" and an approval step (post-incident RCA + logs) to ensure it can't be used to avoid credits. Can you draft language that defines thresholds for emergency (e.g., security CVE with active exploit, critical data-loss risk) and the review process?

Goal: craft a single-page compromise Redwood can send back that will be acceptable to procurement without pushing pricing. We can suggest the $15k onboarding credit (I think that's reasonable) in exchange for keeping the monthly cap at 30% — or we can move the cap to 40% and ask for a 12-month committed minimum spend to offset.

Thanks — Laura

Laura / Marissa — ran a quick model and attached credit-impact-model.xlsx. High level: 

- Moving cap from 30% -> 40% increases expected maximum monthly credit liability by ~33% on an invoice basis. For BlueCrest's projected onboarding ARR, the expected cost under a conservative outage scenario (~2x historical monthly tail events) is approximately $27k net present during the first 12 months versus $20k under our 30% cap.
- Adding a 6-hour hard cap on scheduled maintenance increases operational overhead (~$1.5k/month incremental) for reporting and scheduling tooling, and reduces our maintenance flexibility (we'd need to avoid some low-risk maintenance windows).

Options to bridge: 
A) Keep 30% monthly cap, accept the 6-hour scheduled maintenance cap, and provide a $15k one-time onboarding credit (commercial concession).
B) Move to 40% monthly cap but require a 12-month committed minimum spend at a 12% higher rate (effectively protects us economically).

I prefer Option A to keep procurement happy without touching pricing. I've flagged the numbers in the attached spreadsheet.

Ben
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@bluecrest.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, BlueCrest Legal <legal@bluecrest.io>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final offer: scoped uptime/latency commitments and remedy buckets (BlueCrest)

Samira — thanks for the candid back-and-forth. Based on internal review (Ben and Marissa looped) here's a final, scoping-first offer we can commit to in the contract. If this is acceptable we'll exchange final redlines and push to DocuSign.

1) Uptime: 99.92% uptime floor for BlueCrest on a Dedicated reserved capacity plan, defined on a monthly basis.

2) Scheduled maintenance: hard cap of 6 hours/month that can impact production endpoints. All scheduled maintenance will be posted in the customer portal with 48-hour notice. Monthly maintenance-hours will be reported in the monthly operations summary.

3) Emergency maintenance: defined as work required to remediate a verified security exploit, active data-loss risk, or issues causing persistent incorrect model outputs that threaten customer data integrity. Emergency maintenance hours will be tracked and justified; both parties will conduct a post-incident review with logs and timeline within 7 calendar days. This review is the approval gate for any emergency maintenance exclusion from credits.

4) Latency: baseline P95 <= 200ms for the interactive inference endpoints we discussed. We will run a 3-month pilot at your production profile; if performance certification is achieved for the specific model family within that pilot, Redwood will agree to revisit a 150ms target and sign an addendum for certified models only.

5) Credit/remedy buckets (monthly): 
   - Monthly uptime >= 99.92%: no credit.
   - Monthly uptime < 99.92% and >= 99.85%: 10% credit of monthly invoice.
   - Monthly uptime < 99.85% and >= 99.5%: 25% credit of monthly invoice.
   - Monthly uptime < 99.5%: 50% credit of monthly invoice.
   - Monthly credit cap: 30% of the monthly invoice.

6) Commercial concession: Redwood will provide a one-time onboarding credit of $15,000 applied to the first invoice.

7) Escrow/visibility: we will supply a monthly operations summary (uptime, maintenance hours, incident log, latency percentiles) and provide a shared dashboard for real-time visibility.

If BlueCrest accepts the above, we will: (a) circulate a single redline of the SLA exhibit integrating the language, (b) circulate an MSA with the performance exhibit for signature, and (c) kick off the Dedicated capacity provisioning timeline (~3 weeks to initial availability).

Please confirm acceptance or provide targeted counters. If you want, we can also schedule a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the ops reporting and the pilot measurement plan.

Attachments: Redwood_Final_SLA_Offer.pdf, credit-impact-summary.xlsx

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
